csv_project_name: Design for Twin Peaks Ranch Campground Development
csv_agency: State of Idaho Dept of Parks & Recreation
csv_scope_of_work: The Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation acquired 677 acres in Lemhi County Idaho, and the property currently has no RV facilities. This project would be the first phase of development for 2 RV camping loops with an emphasis for off highway vehicles (OHV s) in one loop and equestrian/basic RV camping in the other. This project will be the first phase of development with the primary focus on overall concept planning, constructing the OHV loop, an entrance kiosk into the park, vault toilets and paved parking where needed. It is anticipated that each loop will have up to 20 RV spots, paved with pull through abilities, toilets and shower facilities if the water and sewer systems can support it. All engineering and construction are anticipated to be contracted via state public works requirements. This project would begin development of 2, RV camping loops with an emphasis for off highway vehicles (OHV s) in one loop and equestrian/basic RV camping in the other. The primary emphasis of OHV camping is a concept IDPR has been pursuing for years. This project would allow that use of a hub for almost 2,000 miles of OHV trails adjacent to the Salmon Challis National Forest
csv_disciplines_requested: Landscape Architecture, Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Surveying/GIS/Mapping, Land Use Planning, Planning/Master Planning, Redevelopment Planning, Environmental Engineering/Planning/Design, Urban Studies/Planning/Design

title: Design for Twin Peaks Ranch Campground Development
short_description: Planning and engineering for first-phase RV campground development with OHV and equestrian loops.
project_scope: First-phase development of a 677-acre park property with two RV camping loops. Planned capacity is up to 20 RV spots per loop, with paved pull-through sites, entrance kiosk, vault toilets, paved parking where needed, and possible toilet and shower facilities subject to water and sewer capacity. One loop is focused on off-highway vehicles and the other on equestrian/basic RV camping. The project also includes overall concept planning and supports access to nearly 2,000 miles of adjacent OHV trails near Salmon-Challis National Forest.
services: Landscape architecture, civil engineering, geotechnical engineering, surveying/GIS/mapping, land use planning, master planning, redevelopment planning, environmental engineering/planning/design, and urban studies/planning/design.
